newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel economic leaders to meet Sunday on budget.
newsitem.headline: Israel economic leaders to meet Sunday on budget.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu will hold a meeting on Sunday to decide whether the 1997 budget must be cut in order to meet the budget deficit target, government officials said.

Officials in the prime minister's office denied a report in the Globes newspaper that any sort of comprehensive package was being contemplated that would include a reduction in interest rates in return for budget cuts.
Finance Minister Dan Meridor and Bank of Israel Governor Jacob Frenkel will also participate in Sunday's meeting.
If a budget cut is recommended it will be brought to the cabinet for a vote only after the Jewish holiday of Passover, which runs from April 21 to 28.

The government had a deficit for the first quarter of 1.37 billion shekels ($405 million). Revenue from taxes in the first quarter totalled 26.8 billion shekels, which economists said was about 250 million shekels below the forecast and equal to a shortfall of 1.5 billion shekels for the year.

A Treasury official said that spending had also been lagging and explained that the budget was based on a 1997 inflation forecast of 11 percent. So far prices have been rising at a slower rate and therefore both spending and revenue figures are slightly inflated, the official said.
Frenkel has been pushing for the Treasury to make cuts immediately to keep the deficit within the target of 2.8 percent of gross domestic product (GDP).
Pessimists among analysts say the government will miss that target by 0.8 percent of GDP, or three to four billion shekels.
The Treasury is reluctant to cut the budget, saying it would slow growth at a time when the economy is weak.
